name: Smith Machine Upright Row
steps: To begin, set the bar on the smith machine to a height that is around the middle of your thighs. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, grasp the bar using a pronated (palms forward) grip that is shoulder width apart. You may need some wrist wraps if using a significant amount of weight.
Lift the barbell up and fully extend your arms with your back straight. There should be a slight bend at the elbows. This is the starting position.

Use your side shoulders to lift the bar as you exhale. The bar should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until it nearly touches your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the bar, your elbows should always be higher than your forearms. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows, keeping them higher than your wrists at all times.
Keep your torso upright and stationary without rocking back.

name: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat
steps: To begin, place a flat bench 2-3 feet behind the smith machine. Then, set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
Position your legs by placing one foot slightly forward under the bar and extending your other leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench. This will be your starting position

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knee as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg and the calf becomes slightly less than 90-degrees (which is the point in which the upper legs are below parallel to the floor). Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knee should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knee is past that imaginary line (if it is past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten your leg again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement.
cues: Keep your chest lifted and push through the midfoot and heel.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes throughout the movement.

name: Standing Calf Raises
steps: Adjust the padded lever of the calf raise machine to fit your height.

Place your shoulders under the pads provided and position your toes facing forward (or using any of the two other positions described at the beginning of the chapter). The balls of your feet should be secured on top of the calf block with the heels extending off it. Push the lever up by extending your hips and knees until your torso is standing erect. The knees should be kept with a slight bend; never locked. Toes should be facing forward, outwards or inwards as described at the beginning of the chapter. This will be your starting position.

Raise your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible and flexing your calf. Ensure that the knee is kept stationary at all times. There should be no bending at any time. Hold the contracted position by a second before you start to go back down.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Keep knees straight but not hyperextended to emphasize the gastrocnemius.
Pause at maximum stretch and peak contraction on every repetition.

name: Standing Leg Curl
steps: Adjust the machine lever to fit your height and lie with your torso bent at the waist facing forward around 30-45 degrees (since an angled position is more favorable for hamstrings recruitment) with the pad of the lever on the back of your right leg (just a few inches under the calves) and the front of the right leg on top of the machine pad.
Keeping the torso bent forward, ensure your leg is fully stretched and grab the side handles of the machine. Position your toes straight. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, curl your right leg up as far as possible without lifting the upper leg from the pad. Once you hit the fully contracted position, hold it for a second.
As you inhale, bring the legs back to the initial position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Perform the same exercise now for the left leg.
cues: Keep the working thigh pressed firmly against the front support pad.
Control the lowering tempo smoothly without hyperextending the knee.

name: Thigh Abductor
steps: To begin, sit down on the abductor machine and select a weight you are comfortable with. When your legs are positioned properly, grip the handles on each side. Your entire upper body (from the waist up) should be stationary. This is the starting position.
Slowly press against the machine with your legs to move them away from each other while exhaling.

Feel the contraction for a second and begin to move your legs back to the starting position while breathing in. Note: Remember to keep your upper body stationary to prevent any injuries from occurring.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Press your back flat into the backrest and avoid using torso momentum to swing the pads.
Pause at peak abduction to fully engage the gluteus medius.

name: Thigh Adductor
steps: To begin, sit down on the adductor machine and select a weight you are comfortable with. When your legs are positioned properly on the leg pads of the machine, grip the handles on each side. Your entire upper body (from the waist up) should be stationary. This is the starting position.
Slowly press against the machine with your legs to move them towards each other while exhaling.

Feel the contraction for a second and begin to move your legs back to the starting position while breathing in. Note: Remember to keep your upper body stationary and avoid fast jerking motions in order to prevent any injuries from occurring.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
cues: Keep your upper body completely still without leaning forward or gripping excessively.
Squeeze the legs together under control without letting the weight stack slam.

name: Catch and Overhead Throw
steps: Stand facing a wall or partner holding a medicine ball in both hands.
Bring the ball behind your head to fully stretch the lats and torso.
Forcefully throw the ball forward overhead, catch the rebound, and immediately reset.
cues: Follow through with the throw and brace core to absorb the catch.
Use full body extension rather than isolating only the arms.

name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
steps: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.
Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Explode through triple extension of ankles, knees, and hips.
Release the ball smoothly overhead without overextending your lower spine.

name: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw
steps: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet.
Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up.
As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you.
cues: Initiate power from explosive hip extension rather than pulling with the arms.
Land softly on bent knees to absorb impact upon completion of the throw.

name: Weighted Crunches
steps: Lie flat on your back with your feet flat on the ground or resting on a bench with your knees bent at a 90 degree angle.
Hold a weight to your chest, or you may hold it extended above your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now, exhale and slowly begin to roll your shoulders off the floor. Your shoulders should come up off the floor about 4 inches while your lower back remains on the floor.
At the top of the movement, flex your abdominals and hold for a brief pause.
Then inhale and slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
cues: Brace your core tightly as if preparing for a punch and avoid arching the lower back.
Exhale forcefully through pursed lips during the concentric contraction.

name: Chin-Up
steps: Grip the pull-up bar with a supinated (underhand) grip slightly narrower than shoulder width.
Pull your torso upward until your chin is over the bar, driving elbows down and back.
Lower under complete control to full arm extension.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid kicking your legs or using excessive swinging momentum.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from an overhead pull-up bar with arms fully extended.
Without swinging, raise your straight legs until parallel to the floor or higher.
Pause briefly and lower slowly to complete each rep.
cues: Brace your core tightly as if preparing for a punch and avoid swinging.
Tilt pelvis slightly posterior at the apex to fully recruit lower abdominals.

name: Gironda Sternum Chins
steps: Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, arms extended, and lean back into an arched spine.
Pull upward while leaning back further until your chest and sternum contact the bar.
Pause and squeeze lats and upper back hard, then lower under control to arm extension.
cues: Keep spine arched and head tilted back throughout the movement.
Lead with elbows pulling down toward your hips.

name: Gorilla Chin/Crunch
steps: Hang from a chin-up bar using an underhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Bend your knees to a 90-degree angle with calves parallel to the floor.
Pull yourself up while simultaneously crunching your knees upward until nose reaches bar height and knees reach chest level.
Slowly lower under control back to the starting hanging position.
cues: Synchronize the chin-up pull with the abdominal knee crunch.
Avoid swinging or using kipping momentum.

name: Hanging Pike (Toes to Bar)
steps: Hang from an overhead pull-up bar with feet together and arms fully extended.
Contract abdominals to pull straight legs upward in a pike until your toes or shins touch the bar overhead.
Slowly lower legs back down under control without swinging.
cues: Brace your core tightly as if preparing for a punch and avoid arching the lower back.
Avoid using swing or kip momentum; lift with abdominal control.

name: Kipping Muscle Up
steps: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings.
Begin with a movement swinging your legs backward slightly.

Counter that movement by swinging your legs forward and up, jerking your chin and chest back, pulling yourself up with both arms as you do so. As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement.
Maintaining control and stability, extend through the elbow to complete the motion.
Use care when lowering yourself to the ground.
cues: Drive hips high toward the rings to facilitate an aggressive forward transition.
Press out smoothly to full elbow lockout at the top of the dip.

name: Muscle Up
steps: Grip the rings using a false grip, with the base of your palms on top of the rings. Initiate a pull up by pulling the elbows down to your side, flexing the elbows.

As you reach the top position of the pull-up, pull the rings to your armpits as you roll your shoulders forward, allowing your elbows to move straight back behind you. This puts you into the proper position to continue into the dip portion of the movement.
Maintaining control and stability, extend through the elbow to complete the motion.
Use care when lowering yourself to the ground.
cues: Keep the false grip secure to facilitate a smooth transition over the rings.
Keep rings close to the body and press straight down into the dip finish.

name: One Arm Chin-Up
steps: For this exercise, start out by placing a towel around a chin up bar.
Grab the chin-up bar with your palm facing you. One hand will be grabbing the chin-up bar and the other will be grabbing the towel.
Bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid using excessive momentum or swinging your torso.

name: One Handed Hang
steps: Grab onto a chinup bar with one hand, using a pronated grip. Keep your feet on the floor or a step. Allow the majority of your weight to hang from that hand, while keeping your feet on the ground. Hold for 10-20 seconds and switch sides.
cues: Engage your grip tightly and keep your hanging shoulder packed and stable.
Breathe steadily and avoid violent swaying.

name: Ring Dips
steps: Grip a ring in each hand, and then take a small jump to help you get into the starting position with your arms locked out.
Begin by flexing the elbow, lowering your body until your arms break 90 degrees. Avoid swinging, and maintain good posture throughout the descent.
Reverse the motion by extending the elbow, pushing yourself back up into the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Keep the rings turned slightly out at the top of the lockout for joint stabilization.
Control the lowering phase without letting the rings drift away from your torso.

name: Rocky Pull-Ups/Pulldowns
steps: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using a wide grip.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back and sticking your chest out. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.

Now repeat the same movements as described above except this time your torso will remain straight as you go up and the bar will touch the back of the neck instead of the upper chest. Tip: Use the head to lean forward slightly as it will help you properly execute this portion of the exercise.
Once you have lowered yourself back down to the starting position, repeat the exercise for the prescribed amount of repetitions in your program.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid using excessive momentum or swinging your torso.

name: Rope Climb
steps: Grab the rope with both hands above your head. Pull down on the rope as you take a small jump.
Wrap the rope around one leg, using your feet to pinch the rope. Reach up as high as possible with your arms, gripping the rope tightly.
Release the rope from your feet as you pull yourself up with your arms, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Resecure your feet on the rope, and then stand up to take another high hold on the rope. Continue until you reach the top of the rope.
To lower yourself, loosen the grip of your feet on the rope as you slide down using a hand over hand motion.
cues: Rely on the leg lock to bear your weight rather than exhausting your grip.
Descend hand-under-hand slowly without sliding down and burning your hands.

name: V-Bar Pullup
steps: Start by placing the middle of the V-bar in the middle of the pull-up bar (assuming that the pull-up station you are using does not have neutral grip handles). The V-Bar handles will be facing down so that you can hang from the pull-up bar through the use of the handles.

Once you securely place the V-bar, take a hold of the bar from each side and hang from it. Stick your chest out and lean yourself back slightly in order to better engage the lats. This will be your starting position.

Using your lats, pull your torso up while leaning your head back slightly so that you do not hit yourself with the chin-up bar. Continue until your chest nearly touches the V-bar. Exhale as you execute this motion.
After a second hold on the contracted position, slowly lower your body back to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid using excessive momentum or swinging your torso.

name: Weighted Pull Ups
steps: Attach a weight to a dip belt and secure it around your waist. Grab the pull-up bar with the palms of your hands facing forward. For a medium grip, your hands should be spaced at shoulder width. Both arms should be extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip.
You'll want to bring your torso back about 30 degrees while creating a curvature in your lower back and sticking your chest out. This will be your starting position.
Now, exhale and pull your torso up until your head is above your hands. Concentrate on squeezing yourshoulder blades back and down as you reach the top contracted position.
After a brief moment at the top contracted position, inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position with your arms extended and your lats fully stretched.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid using excessive momentum or swinging your torso.

name: Wide-Grip Rear Pull-Up
steps: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using a wide grip.

As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar, bring your torso forward and head so that there is an imaginary line from the pull-up bar to the back of your neck. This is your starting position.

Pull your torso up until the bar is near the back of your neck. To do this, draw the shoulders and upper arms down and back while slightly leaning your head forward. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Concentrate on squeezing the back muscles once you reach the full contracted position. The upper torso should remain stationary as it moves through space and only the arms should move. The forearms should do no other work other than hold the bar.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
cues: Lead the pull with your elbows and initiate with scapular retraction.
Avoid using excessive momentum or swinging your torso.

name: Atlas Stones
steps: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the stone.
Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through your feet to break the stone off the floor.
Lap the stone by sitting back onto your thighs.
Readjust grip over the stone, drive through your hips, and extend upward to load the stone onto the platform.
cues: Maintain maximum torso tension and keep the stone tightly pinned against your chest.
Drive forcefully with the hips to clear the loading height.

name: Car Deadlift
steps: Step between the handles of the frame with feet hip-width apart and grip neutral handles firmly.
Drop hips, chest tall, back arched, and take a deep breath.
Drive forcefully through your heels to extend knees and hips upward.
Lock out hips at the top with shoulders back, then guide the implement to the floor.
cues: Keep your chest lifted and push through the midfoot and heel.
Maintain back tightness and drive hips forward into the lockout.

name: Chain Handle Extension
steps: Clip handles to heavy chains and lie back onto a flat bench.
Position elbows pointing straight up with wrists pronated.
Extend through elbows to lift chain links off the floor to full triceps lockout.
Lower under control, pooling chains back onto the floor before the next rep.
cues: Keep upper arms stationary pointing perpendicular to the floor.
Squeeze triceps hard as accommodating chain load peaks at lockout.

name: Chain Press (Dumbbell Style)
steps: Connect chains to cable stirrup handles and lie back on a flat bench.
Hold handles at chest height with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Press upward forcefully to lockout, lifting more chain off the floor as you extend.
Lower under control until elbows reach bench level.
cues: Retract your shoulder blades and maintain a stable, braced upper back.
Maintain controlled pressing path against variable swinging resistance.

name: Circus Bell (Circus Dumbbell Clean & Press)
steps: Place the circus bell between your feet and grip the thick handle firmly.
Clean the implement to your shoulder using hip drive and support from the assisting hand.
Rack the bell onto your shoulder, dip at the knees, and explosively drive it overhead to full single-arm lockout.
Control the implement back down to the floor safely.
cues: Rest one bell head behind the shoulder to maintain overhead leverage.
Lock out elbow completely and establish balance before lowering.

name: Conan's Wheel
steps: Place the loaded beam in the crooks of your elbows using a Zercher hold and grip your wrist.
Stand up tall, lifting the beam off its support frame.
Walk in a circle taking short, rapid steps with chest high.
Continue walking forward until completing target rotations or hitting failure.
cues: Keep upright posture; avoid leaning back or collapsing forward under load.
Breathe in shallow, rhythmic breaths to keep core braced without holding your breath.

name: Crucifix (Isometric Lateral Hold)
steps: Stand tall holding weights or axes at your sides.
Raise both arms straight out laterally until they are strictly parallel to the floor forming a cross.
Statically hold the arms locked at parallel for maximum time, fighting downward fatigue.
cues: Lock elbows straight and brace core and glutes firmly.
Do not allow arms to dip below shoulder parallel height.

name: Donkey Calf Raises
steps: Bend forward at the waist and place your hands or elbows on a sturdy bench or support for stability.
Position the balls of your feet on a calf block or sturdy raised platform with heels hanging off.
Have your training partner carefully sit straddling your lower back and hips to provide resistance.
Lower your heels down as far as possible to achieve a full calf stretch.
Extend through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible, pausing for peak contraction at the top.
cues: Keep a slight micro-bend in the knees and do not bounce at the bottom.
Ensure your partner's weight is centered over your hips, not directly on the lumbar spine.

name: Medicine Ball Full Twist
steps: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position.
Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner.
For full rotation, you and your partner should twist in the same direction, i.e. counter-clockwise.
Pass the ball to your partner, and both of you can now twist in the opposite direction to repeat the procedure.
cues: Brace your core tightly as if preparing for a punch and avoid arching the lower back.
Exhale forcefully through pursed lips during the concentric contraction.

name: Bench Sprint
steps: Stand facing a bench or box with one foot resting securely on top of the edge.
Push off explosively with the top foot extending through hip and knee.
Switch feet mid-air to land with opposite foot on the bench.
Alternate rapidly in a continuous sprinting rhythm.
cues: Pump your arms actively in coordination with foot contacts.
Land softly on the ball of the foot to absorb impact.

name: Depth Jump Leap
steps: Stand on a low box facing a higher box spaced two to three feet away.
Step off the initial box, land softly on both feet, and rebound immediately with maximum explosive power.
Drive arms upward to jump onto the higher box, absorbing impact through knees upon landing.
cues: Minimize ground contact time between landing and the explosive takeoff.
Land softly with flexed knees and hips.

name: Drop Push (Plyo Push-Up Drop)
steps: Assume a push-up position with hands supported on two low platforms 2-3 feet apart.
Drop hands between the blocks to the floor, absorbing the impact into a deep push-up.
Immediately explode upward, pressing hands forcefully back onto the platforms.
cues: Retract your shoulder blades and maintain a stable, braced upper back.
Control the eccentric lowering phase without flaring elbows excessively.

name: Step-up with Knee Raise
steps: Stand facing a box or bench of an appropriate height with your feet together. This will be your starting position.

Begin the movement by stepping up, putting your left foot on the top of the bench. Extend through the hip and knee of your front leg to stand up on the box. As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can.
Reverse this motion to step down off the box, and then repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.
cues: Keep your chest lifted and push through the midfoot and heel.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes throughout the movement.

name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
steps: Loop the band around a solid post and place the opposite end behind your neck, using hands to secure it.
Hinge at the hips, driving your glutes backward while keeping back flat and knees slightly soft.
Extend forcefully through your hips to return to a tall standing lockout.
cues: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding the lumbar back.
Drive the hips forward by actively squeezing your glutes at the top.

name: Band Hip Adductions
steps: Anchor a band to a sturdy post and wrap the loop around the ankle of your outside leg.
Stand tall, holding onto the post for balance if needed.
Pull the resisted leg inward across the midline of your body against band tension.
Slowly control the return to the starting position and repeat.
cues: Keep your pelvis level and avoid tilting the torso sideways.
Initiate movement purely from the inner thigh adductors.

name: Band Skull Crusher
steps: Secure a band to the base of a bench or rack and lie back with the band aligned behind your head.
Hold the band with upper arms vertical and perpendicular to the floor, elbows flexed.
Extend through your elbows to press your hands straight up toward the ceiling.
Pause at lockout and slowly lower hands back down past your forehead.
cues: Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the entire rep.
Avoid flaring elbows excessively outward.

name: Hamstring Stretch with Band
steps: Lie on your back with one leg extended flat on the floor.
Loop a band or belt over the ball of your opposite foot and raise that leg vertically toward the ceiling.
Gently pull the band to create tension in your hamstrings and calves, holding for 15-30 seconds before switching legs.
cues: Keep your pelvis and lower back flat against the floor.
Maintain a straight leg without locking or hyperextending the knee.

name: Hip Extension with Bands
steps: Anchor a band low to a post and attach the other end around your ankle, facing the attachment point.
Hold the post for balance with torso upright.
Keeping working leg straight, kick it directly backward against band resistance.
Squeeze the glute hard at peak extension, then return under control.
cues: Avoid arching the lumbar spine; isolate extension strictly in the glute.
Keep hips square to the post throughout.

name: Hip Flexion with Band
steps: Anchor a band low to a post and attach to one ankle, facing away from the anchor point.
Stand tall and drive the resisted knee upward toward your chest to 90 degrees.
Pause at peak hip flexion, then lower foot back to the starting stance.
cues: Maintain upright torso posture without leaning backward as knee drives high.
Brace standing leg glute for stability.

name: Hip Lift with Band
steps: Lie on the floor inside a rack with a band anchored on both sides directly across your hips.
Bend knees and plant feet flat on the floor at shoulder width.
Drive through your heels to extend hips upward against band resistance.
Pause and squeeze glutes hard at the top, then slowly return to the floor.
cues: Keep your chest lifted and push through the midfoot and heel.
Avoid hyperextending the lumbar spine at peak hip bridge lockout.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
steps: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.
Pull the end of the band down, and place one bent knee into the loop, ensuring it won't slip out. Take a medium to wide grip on the bar. This will be your starting position.

Pull yourself upward by contracting the lats as you flex the elbow. The elbow should be driven to your side. Pull to the front, attempting to get your chin over the bar. Avoid swinging or jerking movements.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
cues: Initiate pull with scapular depression before bending elbows.
Keep core braced to minimize swinging.

name: External Rotation with Band
steps: Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.
Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.
With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a backhand motion, keeping your elbow in place.
Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
cues: Pin your elbow tightly to your side throughout the rotation.
Control both the inward and outward rotation without swinging your torso.

name: Internal Rotation with Band
steps: Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your right side to the band a couple of feet away.
Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.
With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching away from your torso. This will be your starting position.
Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a forehand motion, keeping your elbow in place.
Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout the rotation.
Avoid twisting your torso to compensate for shoulder internal rotation.

name: Pallof Press
steps: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and—if possible—position the cable to shoulder height. If not, a low pulley will suffice.
With your side to the cable, grab the handle with both hands and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable.
With your feet positioned hip-width apart and knees slightly bent, hold the cable to the middle of your chest. This will be your starting position.
Press the cable away from your chest, fully extending both arms. You core should be tight and engaged.
Hold the repetition for several seconds before returning to the starting position.
At the conclusion of the set, repeat facing the other direction.
cues: Brace your core tightly as if preparing for a punch and avoid arching the lower back.
Exhale forcefully through pursed lips during the concentric contraction.

name: Pallof Press With Rotation
steps: Connect a standard handle to a tower, and position the cable to shoulder height.

With your side to the cable, grab the handle with one hand and step away from the tower. You should be approximately arm's length away from the pulley, with the tension of the weight on the cable. Align outstretched arm with cable.
With your feet positioned hip-width apart, pull the cable into your chest and grab the handle with your other hand. Both hands should be on the handle at this time.
Facing forward, press the cable away from your chest. You core should be tight and engaged.
Keeping your hips straight, twist your torso away from the pulley until you get a full quarter rotation.
Maintain your rigid stance and straight arms. Return to the neutral position in a slow and controlled manner. Your arms should be extended in front of you.
With the side tension still engaging your core, bring your hands to your chest and immediately press outward to a fully extended position. This constitutes one rep.
Repeat to failure.
Then, reposition and repeat the same series of movements on the opposite side.
cues: Rotate strictly through the thoracic spine while locking the pelvis and hips forward.
Keep arms straight and core rigidly braced during the rotation.

name: Seated Band Hamstring Curl
steps: Secure a band close to the ground and place a bench a couple feet away from it.
Seat yourself on the bench and secure the band behind your ankles, beginning with your legs straight. This will be your starting position.
Flex the knees, bringing your feet towards the bench. You may need to lean back slightly to keep your feet from striking the floor.
Pause at the completion of the movement, and then slowly return to the starting position.
cues: Squeeze the hamstrings hard at full knee flexion.
Control the elastic return without letting the band snap your legs forward.

name: Keg Load
steps: To load kegs, place the desired number a distance from the loading platform, typically 30-50 feet.
Begin by grabbing the close handle of the first keg, tilting it onto its side to grab the opposite edge of the bottom of the keg. Lift the keg up to your chest.

The higher you can place the keg, the faster you should be able to move to the platform. Shouldering is usually not allowed. Be sure to keep a firm hold on the keg. Move as quickly as possible to the platform, and load it, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles to get it as high as possible.
Return to the starting position to retrieve the next keg, and repeat until the event is completed.
cues: Brace your core tightly when lapping and picking the awkward implement.
Extend aggressively through the hips at the platform to load the object.

name: Sandbag Load
steps: To load sandbags or other objects, begin with the implements placed a distance from the loading platform, typically 50 feet.

Begin by lifting the sandbag. Sandbags are extremely awkward, and the manner of lifting them can vary depending on the particular sandbag used. Reach as far around it as possible, extending through the hips and knees to pull it up high. Shouldering is usually not allowed.
Move as quickly as possible to the platform, and load it, extending through your hips, knees, and ankles to get it as high as possible. Place it onto the platform, ensuring it doesn't fall off.
Return to the starting position to retrieve the next sandbag, and repeat until the event is completed.
cues: Keep your chest lifted and push through the midfoot and heel.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes throughout the movement.

name: Sled Drag - Harness
steps: To begin, load the sled with the desired weight and attach the pulling strap. You can pull with handles, use a harness, or attach the pulling strap to a weight belt.
Whether pulling forwards or backwards, lean in the direction of travel and progress by extending through the hips and knees.
cues: Maintain a steady torso lean and drive hard through the balls of your feet.
Keep your core engaged and steps rhythmic without breaking posture.

name: Sled Forward Drag with Press
aliases: Weight Sled Drag with Chest Press
steps: Attach strap handles to a loaded sled and stand facing away from the sled.
Take a step forward leaning your body into the straps.
With each forward stride, press both handles forward vigorously in a chest press motion.
Continue marching forward pressing with each step across the designated distance.
cues: Drive forcefully off the balls of your feet on every step.
Time arm press synchronously with lead foot plant.
